name: Draven, Glorious Executioner
howItPlays: You attach Spinning Axes and other gear to your units, pick fights you can win, and draw a card every time you win a combat to keep your hand full. You use that steady card draw to keep replacing your attackers until your bigger units take over the game.
whyYou: You like combat math and want every attack to be a real decision about gear, positioning, and what your opponent can answer with. You're fine with a slower start if it means your card draw snowballs once your key units start winning fights, and you don't mind that a few matchups punish you hard if you fall behind early. If you'd rather out-think an opponent turn by turn than just race them, Draven gives you plenty to chew on.
ratingNotes: Legend ability: when you win a combat, draw 1 card. pace 5: riftbound.gg's guide says the deck 'snowballs' once key units stick and 'doesn't fare well when forced to play from behind,' pointing to a midgame plan rather than an early rush; riftboundguide.com separately describes a faster 'Miracle' combo variant built around cost-reduction cards, so this number reflects the more common standard build. stance 4: riftbound.gg frames the deck as 'a control, reactive environment with a few large units to deal with eventually,' though hextechanalytics.com pushes back that it wants to 'establish the first battlefield' proactively - landed on the reactive side since more sources describe it that way. complexity 7: hextechanalytics.com is explicit that players must count the defender's actual might before committing an axe and track hidden-card setup, and magicalmeta.ink calls the deck 'not the easiest to play but very rewarding.' variance 6.5: hextechanalytics.com calls the deck 'moderately high variance' tied to hidden-card mechanics and equipment-dependent combat, and riftboundguide.com's separate Miracle build adds explosive cost-reduction turns on top of that. Confidence: medium-high, five distinct sources read (a riftbound.gg strategy guide, the riftbound.gg tier list confirming a real Tier 3 placement, hextechanalytics.com, magicalmeta.ink, and riftboundguide.com); they genuinely disagree on the archetype label (reactive midrange vs. tempo vs. aggro-combo), most likely because two different real decklists exist for this Legend, so reviewer should treat archetype as the least certain field here. riftboundguide.com explicitly states 'Draven is not available as a pre-built champion deck,' so starterDeck is null.
